title: Default It
goal: Config::default() must work. One version doesn't compile; of the two that do, one wrote code a derive already writes.
hints: An inherent new() is not the Default trait - Config::default() only exists if the trait is implemented.
When every field's default is the field type's default, the derive writes your impl verbatim.
explanation: Default is a trait, so a plain new() method leaves Config::default() unresolvable (E0599) - traits are contracts, not naming conventions. The manual impl works but reimplements exactly what #[derive(Default)] generates - Clippy's derivable_impls points this out. Zeros and falses ARE the field defaults, so the derive is both shorter and self-maintaining when fields change. Write impls only where the defaults are actually interesting.
